correctness.rationale: For each output coordinate the meet-preserving scalar map has nested principal filters F0 and F1. Pos is equivalent to the threshold of F0 lying coordinatewise at most zero. Con is equivalent to preservation of the 1-level set under joining a vector in {-1,0}^n, forcing the generator of any nonempty F1 to have only -1 and 1 coordinates. Conversely these threshold conditions imply all three axioms. The resulting 2^n type-I or 3^n type-II choices are unique per coordinate, giving (3^n+2^n)^n operations, 3^(n^2) normal ones and the stated asymptotic normal fraction. The actual embedded checker independently exhausts all scalar functions on K3^1 and K3^2, compares accepted and constructed sets and confirms counts; finite enumeration is not substituted for the general proof.

originality.rationale: The motivating primary work proves categorical triple/contact representations for modal Kleene algebras, but neither its inspected axioms nor its representation statements identify the explicit two-threshold coordinate normal form or the exact normal/non-normal spectra for all Cartesian powers of the three-element carrier. Literature and mathematical-record searches under product, ternary matrix, threshold, modal contact and exact-count formulations located no statement implying the new quantitative spectrum. A previously obtained finite-chain result only intersects at one factor; general finite-chain counts do not imply results for non-chain products. Generic representations must be further specialized and their compatibility constraints counted, as done in the proof. Residual priority risk from older three-valued modal-operator classifications is explicitly acknowledged.
residual_risks: Uninspected older literature on meet homomorphisms or many-valued modal operators may encode an equivalent ternary relation normal form.

value.rationale: The direct powers of the three-element Kleene algebra are a canonical infinite family of finite distributive De Morgan/Kleene algebras. A new unique two-threshold normal form classifies every operator satisfying three interacting modal axioms and explains the independent three-state input/output edge encoding for normal boxes. Two exact all-dimension spectra quantify the difference between normal and non-normal modal logics. The asymptotic non-normal fraction n(2/3)^n is a nontrivial qualitative change from chain models and offers a natural size-dependent baseline for modal expansions; these are not arbitrary slices or mere finite table entries.
